title: Restriction of the finite class-relative exceptional adjunction
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and an integer $d\ge0$ with $\dim\overline X\le d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On the small pro-etale sites put $\mathcal C_{T,n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], let $f_{c,n}^{\times}$ be the right adjoint of ordinary etale compact support $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$, and set
$$F_{c,n}=Rp_*j_!,\qquad G_{c,n}=\nu_X^*f_{c,n}^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}$$
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Both $F_{c,n}$ and $G_{c,n}$ preserve these finite-Tor constructible subcategories. For $K\in\mathcal C_{X,n}$ and $L\in\mathcal C_{Y,n}$ the class-relative natural bijections restrict to
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{Y,n}}(F_{c,n}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{X,n}}(K,G_{c,n}L).$$
They define $F_{c,n}\dashv G_{c,n}$, whose unit and counit, under the full inclusions, are the class-relative unit and counit. The compactification comparisons preserve these bijections and satisfy their original cocycle on the constructible domains. No adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale complexes is asserted.

proof.text: For the actual quotient A=ULift(O_E/(varpi^n)), the characteristic p of the base is invertible: its l-adic spectral norm is one since l differs from p, so it is a unit in O_E and in the quotient. HasInvertibleExponent.spec_of_charP gives invertible exponent on Spec k, and pullback gives it on Y. This uses precisely the published coefficient ring, without any coefficient equivalence or change of universe of E.

Use the adopted source theorem constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.Derived.CompactifFiniteTor for every compactification. It proves exactly preservation of the native fixed-ModuleCat finite-Tor constructible predicate, already used in the statement, without requiring a supplied dimension bound. Use constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek in the adopted UpperShriekFiniteness module for the canonical comparison-transported right adjoint. For an arbitrary supplied etale adjoint (G,adj), adj.rightAdjointUniq identifies G with the canonical etale adjoint after the canonical compact-support isomorphism; apply comparison pullback to this isomorphism and transport finite-Tor membership through it. These are the already proved native preservation APIs underlying the recorded exceptional operation, so no new geometric preservation lemma is stated.

Quasi-compactness of Y follows from its finite-type structure map. The canonical ordinary etale exceptional adjoint preserves bounded-below complexes. Transport this lower bound to the supplied G by the same unique-adjoint isomorphism, and precompose with derived comparison direct image, which preserves a lower bound. Apply lem-sf-specified-comparison-class-construction to obtain the normalized class datum for this exact adjunction. Convert the fixed class record to ComparisonClassAdjunction field by field.

In the private proved restrictClass helper, wrap each class Hom equivalence and its inverse with ObjectProperty.homMk. Source and target naturality follow by applying the inclusion and the original naturality equations. Apply Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. Its Hom-equivalence equation gives the required retained Hom map; its unit and counit component formulas give precisely the transposes of identity in the class datum.

Lift each class comparison component and inverse with ObjectProperty.isoMk. The original naturality equation gives a natural isomorphism between the restricted functors. Full-subcategory hom_ext reduces comparison-Hom compatibility, identity and cocycle to the original class equations. No bounds for additional compactifications are needed because Step 2 preserves the native finite-Tor domain for every compactification at once.
